title: Sustainable Cities: BedZED and Curitiba
welcome_lead: From south London eco-houses to bus-rapid Brazil, explore models of sustainable urban living.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: sustainable urbanism, BedZED, Curitiba BRT and Brundtland.
final_note: You have visited eco-experiments and city-scale systems. Sustainability is achievable but requires holistic design.

concepts.def: Sustainable development is 'meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs' (1987).
Beddington Zero Energy Development in south London, completed 2002, a low-energy eco-village of 100 homes.
Bus Rapid Transit, a high-capacity bus system using dedicated lanes pioneered in Curitiba in 1974.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 1987 Brundtland Report Our Common Future set the now-classic definition of sustainable development. Applied to cities, it implies balancing environmental quality, social equity and economic vitality across generations.

BedZED's mixed-use design, super-insulation, passive solar gain, on-site combined heat and power and recycled materials achieved substantial cuts in energy and water use relative to UK averages. Post-occupancy evaluation revealed gaps between design intentions and behaviour — useful lessons for replication.

Mayor Jaime Lerner's Curitiba pioneered BRT in 1974, integrating land-use planning with rapid bus corridors carrying around 2 million passengers a day. Other features include parks built on floodable land, generous green space per capita and waste-for-bus-fares programmes in low-income areas.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.

options: LICs have higher urbanisation rates because they have more cities than HICs.
HICs urbanised earlier and are now near saturation (80%+ urban); LICs are still in the rapid urbanisation phase, with high rural-urban migration and urban natural increase.
Correlation and causation are the same thing.
